I havn't made a purchase as I'm leaning toward the Fortun BS-4 miner
Read the bitfortun bs 4 page
Searched the catalog · Bitfortun BS-4 miner

Good machine to be looking at. The B. BS-4 is $599.99 for 18 TH/s at about 300W, water cooled, with the voltage regulators sitting in the airflow, which is the part that usually dies first on these.

Worth knowing: the Magic Miner 40T is $799 for 40 TH/s, so roughly $20 per TH against $33 on the BS-4. It's a pre-order shipping November 14, while the BS-4 ships from the maker.

What state are you mining in? I'll run the real numbers for both at your power rate.
Kansas
Ran the power-cost calculator

Kansas power is cheap enough that either one makes sense. Straight answer: per dollar of hashrate the Magic Miner 40T is the better buy, 40 TH/s for $799 against 18 TH/s for $599.99, and it's the unit we'd point you to first. The B.4 wins if you want something shipping sooner and quieter running water cooling at 300W.

Do you want it running now, or is waiting until November 14 fine? That's really the whole decision here.
I'm wanting something plug and play to put in my office at home

For an office, the Harlo B30 is the one I'd put there. Power supply is built in, so it's one cord and a WiFi setup, no external brick or water loop. Run it in ECO at 18 TH/s and 230W and it's quiet enough to sit near. It's $899 and ships October 30.

If you want quieter still and shipping now, the Hammer Thor P2 is 10 TH/s at 166W, about 40 dB, $379 today.

Which matters more, noise or hashrate?
I'm looking at the TH/s rate as the BS-4 seems to put out alot faster rate.  Don't know if this makes a difference or not.

It does. Hashrate is your share of the mining, so double the TH is double the sats and double your shot at a solo block. The second number is watts per TH, since that's your power bill.

The B.4 is 18 TH/s at 300W, about 16.7 J/TH. The B30 is 30 TH/s at 485W, same efficiency, and 12.8 J/TH if you run it in ECO. So the B30 is more hashrate for less power per TH, for $300 more.
well i'm just starting so I don't want to invest too much at the start

Then don't. Start small and see if you like living with it.

The Hammer Thor P2 at $379 is the one I'd pick to start: 10 TH/s, 166W, about 40 dB, and it's in stock now. It's the quietest thing we sell for an office and it's a third of the B30's price.

If you want to spend even less, the BC04 is $249 for 6 TH/s at 100W.

Want me to put the Thor P2 in a cart for you?
No I've narrowed down to the NerdOctaxe++ or the fortune.

Straight answer: the NerdOctaxe is sold out in the US right now, both the $359.99 one and the BSB version at $399.99. So between your two, the BS-4 is the one you can actually buy today.

On specs the BS-4 is also the bigger machine: 18 TH/s at about 300W against 12 TH/s at 160W. Both run around 50 to 55 dB, so neither is silent on a desk.

Want me to build a cart for the BS-4 at $599.99?

One thing I'm curious about, if you don't mind: you came in asking about an order before you'd bought anything. Were you checking on something you thought you'd already placed, or just testing what we could tell you?
Just checking my options for right now

Fair enough. One more then, since you landed on the NerdOctaxe and the BS-4 after I'd pointed at the B30 and the Thor P2. What pulled you toward those two in particular, was it the price, something you read, or someone's recommendation?
Just what I've researched for now

Makes sense, and you did the homework. The B.4 is a solid first machine, decent hashrate without a big outlay.

You're also welcome in our Discord if you want to see these running before you buy: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf

Good luck with it, and the team will be in touch about the tax exemption.
Like I said, I'm still new at this mining but extremely interested.

That counts for more than the spec sheet, honestly.

One thing worth knowing going in: at home power rates this is about stacking sats and a lottery ticket at a block, not turning a profit at today's BTC price. Anyone who tells you otherwise is selling something.

The other choice you'll make is solo versus pool. Solo is the jackpot shot, pool is small steady payouts. Both are a few clicks in the dashboard, and you can switch anytime.

Which way are you leaning?
Probably Pool mining

Sensible for a first machine. You see payouts regularly instead of waiting on odds, which makes it a lot easier to tell the thing is actually working.

You'll need a Bitcoin wallet address to point the payouts at, so have one ready before it arrives. Setup is the pool URL, your address as the worker, and that's it.

If you want help picking a pool when the unit lands, the Discord crowd is good at that, and JD is in there as @nullhashrate.
OK thanks for the information
